classification.difficultyReason: The hardest essential demand is coordinating the component breakpoints and signed slopes to construct continuous sums or differences across three intervals. The straight-line structure is explicitly signposted, so this requires routine linked procedures.

content.prompt: Sketch these absolute value sums and differences. As absolute value graphs are made up of linear sections, your sums and differences should be made up of straight-line sections.

answer.worked:
Add the component ordinates at their vertices.

At $x=-1$:
$$\begin{align*}y&=|-1+1|+|-1-2|\\y&=0+3\\y&=3\end{align*}$$
At $x=2$:
$$\begin{align*}y&=|2+1|+|2-2|\\y&=3+0\\y&=3\end{align*}$$
The component slopes add to $-2$, $0$ and $2$ on the three intervals separated by $x=-1$ and $x=2$. Join the vertices horizontally and continue the outer rays.

At $x=-2$:
$$\begin{align*}y&=|-2-1|-|-2+2|\\y&=3-0\\y&=3\end{align*}$$
At $x=1$:
$$\begin{align*}y&=|1-1|-|1+2|\\y&=0-3\\y&=-3\end{align*}$$
At $x=0$:
$$\begin{align*}y&=|0-1|-|0+2|\\y&=1-2\\y&=-1\end{align*}$$
The component slopes subtract to $0$, $-2$ and $0$ on the intervals separated by $x=-2$ and $x=1$. Join the vertices with a descending straight segment and continue the horizontal outer rays.

answer.worked:
Add the component ordinates at their vertices.

At $x=-\frac12$:
$$\begin{align*}y&=\left|2\left(-\frac12\right)+1\right|+\left|-\frac12-1\right|\\y&=0+\frac32\\y&=\frac32\end{align*}$$
At $x=1$:
$$\begin{align*}y&=|2(1)+1|+|1-1|\\y&=3+0\\y&=3\end{align*}$$
At $x=0$:
$$\begin{align*}y&=|2(0)+1|+|0-1|\\y&=1+1\\y&=2\end{align*}$$
The component slopes add to $-3$, $1$ and $3$ on the intervals separated by $x=-\frac12$ and $x=1$. Join the vertices with a rising straight segment and continue the outer rays.
